newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk settles with independent producers.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk settles with independent producers.

text.p: Niagara Mohawk Power Corp. said Monday it has tentatively settled a dispute with 19 independent power producers, agreeing in principle to restructure or terminate 44 power purchase contracts.

The utility has more than 150 power purchase contracts with non-regulated generators, spokesman Nicholas Ashooh said, noting that the 44 contracts represent more than 90 percent of its above-market power costs.

Niagara Mohawk said that under the agreement, it expects to pay the 19 power producers about $3.6 million in cash and or debt securities, and 46 million common shares. It said the stock will represent about 25 percent of its fully diluted common shares.
In addition, Niagara Mohawk said, the company and the producers will enter into new agreements that would compensate the producers and hedge the prices for specified amounts of power.
Niagara Mohawk estimates it will realise savings of up to $5 billion over 15 years, with those savings occurring in the second half of that period.

Under the agreement, electricity prices for all customer classes would be reduced, with larger reductions allocated to large commercial and industrial customers to retain and attract jobs in upstate New York, the utility said.
Niagara Mohawk cautioned that there are still important issues that must be resolved, including negotiations with each independent producer on specific terms of the new price-hedging agreements.
Niagra Mohawk's stock lost 87.5 cents to end at $9.375 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
